title: Split geometric fibres and the finite fpqc covering test
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\Omega/k$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(\Omega)$ with the Krull topology. Use [def-weil-size-convention]. For an ind-etale $k$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], put $B_\Omega=\Omega\otimes_kB$ and $F_k(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(B,\Omega)$, topologized by restriction to finite etale subalgebras, with left action $g\cdot f=g\circ f$. Spectra and affine fibre products have their usual meanings [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-fibre-product].

The algebra $B_\Omega$ is ind-etale over $\Omega$. Every point of $\operatorname{Spec}B_\Omega$ has residue field canonically isomorphic to $\Omega$ as an $\Omega$-algebra. The assignment
$$f\longmapsto\ker\bigl(B_\Omega\to\Omega,\ a\otimes b\longmapsto a f(b)\bigr)$$
is a homeomorphism from $F_k(B)$ onto $|\operatorname{Spec}B_\Omega|$. It is natural under all $k$-algebra maps between ind-etale algebras. The corresponding natural homeomorphism $F_\Omega(B_\Omega)\cong F_k(B)$ is given by restriction along $b\mapsto1\otimes b$; on the right the $G$-action is forgotten. Here $F_\Omega$ uses the identical finite-subalgebra construction with the separably closed field $\Omega$ as its own separable closure.

For an arbitrary small family of $k$-algebra maps $B\to B_a$ between ind-etale algebras, the scheme family $\{\operatorname{Spec}B_a\to\operatorname{Spec}B\}_a$ is an fpqc covering [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] if and only if some finite subfamily of the induced maps $F_k(B_a)\to F_k(B)$ is jointly surjective. Empty algebras, empty families, and the empty target are included. All assertions also apply with $k=\Omega$.

source.place: Definition 4.1.1 and Example 4.1.10, pp. 27–28: split base change, spectrum topology, and fpqc coverings.

proof.text: Put $A=\Omega\otimes_kB$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], $A$ is ind-etale over $\Omega$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-geometric-fibre-construction] with base field $\Omega$ and separable closure $\Omega$ to write $A$ as the directed union of its finite etale $\Omega$-subalgebras $C$. Each $C$ is $\Omega^n$, including $n=0$, by clause 1 of [det-pe-condensed-point-basis]. For a prime $q$ of $A$, its contraction to $C$ is a coordinate kernel by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields]. Hence $C/(q\cap C)=\Omega$ through the structural map. Every element of $A/q$ is represented in some $C$, so $\Omega\to A/q$ is surjective; it is injective because $q$ is proper and $\Omega$ is a field. Thus $A/q=\Omega$ canonically as an $\Omega$-algebra. In particular $q$ is maximal and its residue field is canonically $\Omega$.

On $C\cong\Omega^n$, an $\Omega$-algebra map to $\Omega$ sends the orthogonal coordinate idempotents to zeros and ones, and exactly one to one, because their sum is one. It is that coordinate projection. Thus the kernel map identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Omega\text{-alg}}(C,\Omega)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$, with both finite discrete topologies; discreteness on the spectrum is [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields]. These identifications commute with restriction: $\ker(h\circ u)=u^{-1}(\ker h)$. By [lem-sfb-field-geometric-fibre-construction], $F_\Omega(A)$ is the inverse limit of these finite Hom sets, and by [lem-a1-filtered-spectrum-topological-limit] $|\operatorname{Spec}A|$ is the inverse limit of the spectra, since $A=\varinjlim C$. The coordinate kernel maps therefore induce a homeomorphism $F_\Omega(A)\to|\operatorname{Spec}A|$, sending $h$ to $\ker h$.

Define $R(h)(b)=h(1\otimes b)$ and $S(f)(a\otimes b)=a f(b)$. The latter extends to $A$ because the displayed formula is $k$-balanced and multiplicative, preserves one, and is $\Omega$-linear. The identities $RS(f)=f$ and $SR(h)(a\otimes b)=a h(1\otimes b)=h(a\otimes b)$ show they are inverse. To check both topologies, use the finite-subalgebra bases from [lem-sfb-field-geometric-fibre-construction]. For a finite $k$-subalgebra $B_i$, choose a finite generating list. The images $1\otimes b$ of that list lie in one finite $\Omega$-subalgebra $C$ of $A$; thus $R(h)|_{B_i}$ is determined by $h|_C$, so $R$ is continuous. Conversely, take a finite generating list for a finite $\Omega$-subalgebra $C\subset A$, and write its generators as finite sums $\sum a_j\otimes b_j$. The finitely many $b_j$ lie in one finite etale $k$-subalgebra $B_i\subset B$. Then $S(f)|_C$ is determined by $f|_{B_i}$, so $S$ is continuous. These are maps between finite discrete restriction sets, hence the stated factorisations prove continuity. Composing $S$ with step 2 gives exactly the homeomorphism $f\mapsto\ker(a\otimes b\mapsto a f(b))$.

For a $k$-algebra map $\alpha:B\to D$, direct evaluation on pure tensors gives $S_B(f\circ\alpha)=S_D(f)\circ(\mathrm{id}_\Omega\otimes\alpha)$. Taking kernels contracts primes along $\mathrm{id}_\Omega\otimes\alpha$, which is the corresponding spectrum map [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Restriction satisfies $R_B(h\circ(\mathrm{id}\otimes\alpha))=R_D(h)\circ\alpha$. Thus both homeomorphisms are natural, with precisely the claimed restriction map and underlying space $F_k(B)$ after forgetting its action. The calculations also apply for $k=\Omega$.

Every map $B\to B_a$ is ind-etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], since both algebras are ind-etale over $k$. It is consequently weakly etale. Under [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] this means its induced affine scheme morphism is weakly etale, and by [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism] that morphism is flat. This applies to every index, not only the eventual finite selection, and to the base-changed algebras over $\Omega$.

For this family of flat maps between affines, the definition [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering] implies that any fpqc covering has a finite subfamily jointly surjective on $\operatorname{Spec}B$: take its affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and enlarge the finitely many source opens to their whole source schemes. Conversely, suppose a finite set $J$ of indices is jointly surjective. For any affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}D\subset\operatorname{Spec}B$, the inverse image of $V$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ is the open fibre product by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], affine with ring $B_a\otimes_BD$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. For $a\in J$ these finitely many affine opens map onto $V$ jointly. Together with step 5 this is exactly the fpqc definition for the entire family. The argument works verbatim over $\Omega$.

Suppose the original family is fpqc. Choose the finite set $J$ of step 6. The subfamily indexed by $J$ is itself fpqc by that step. Its base change to $\operatorname{Spec}A$ remains fpqc by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its source over index $a$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_k B_a)$: the tensor identification sends $(a\otimes b)\otimes d$ to $a\otimes\alpha_a(b)d$, with inverse $a\otimes d\mapsto(a\otimes1)\otimes d$. This finite family is jointly surjective on spectra by the covering definition [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The natural kernel homeomorphisms of steps 2–4 identify its point maps with $F_k(B_a)\to F_k(B)$, so this same finite $J$ is jointly surjective on the geometric fibres.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, finite covering criterion; base-change axiom from Stacks 022D

proof.text: Conversely, suppose a finite $J$ is jointly surjective on the $F_k$ spaces. Steps 2–4 make the corresponding maps $\operatorname{Spec}(\Omega\otimes_kB_a)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ jointly surjective. The map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective since each field spectrum has one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], its base change $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is surjective. Given $p\in\operatorname{Spec}B$, choose a point $q$ above it and then a point above $q$ in one source with index $a\in J$. Its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ maps to $p$, by the commuting base-change square. Thus $J$ is jointly surjective on the original spectra, and step 6 proves that the whole family is fpqc. If $B=0$, all $B_a=0$, every spectrum and fibre is empty, and $J=\varnothing$ satisfies both tests. If $B\ne0$, [lem-sfb-field-geometric-fibre-construction] gives $F_k(B)\ne\varnothing$, so an empty family satisfies neither test. Zero source algebras contribute empty spaces. This also checks all assertions for $k=\Omega$.

Step checks: step 1 shows Omega⊗B is ind-etale and a directed union of copies of Omega^n (finite etale algebras over a separably closed field, n=0 allowed), so A/q = Omega canonically. Step 2 identifies Hom with Spec at the finite stages by the idempotent argument, with compatible kernels, and applies the filtered-spectrum limit to a small, nonempty directed poset. Step 3 checks that S(f)(a⊗b) = a f(b) is k-balanced, that RS and SR are identities, and that R and S are continuous through finite generators. Step 4 checks naturality on pure tensors, which is Spec(id⊗α). Step 5 gets flatness of every arrow from the ind-etale stability node and the 'equivalently flat' clause. Step 6 proves fpqc iff finite joint surjectivity: the preimage of an affine open is open (open-immersion base change) and equals Spec(D⊗_B B_a). Step 7 uses base change of the finite subfamily (axioms clause 3) and the tensor identification (a⊗b)⊗d ↦ a⊗α(b)d, which I checked against the projections. Step 8 lifts points through the surjective Spec A → Spec B. Edge cases checked: B=0 (all B_a=0, J empty), the empty family with B nonzero (F_k(B) is nonempty), k=Omega, B=k, and B a finite separable L. No SGA is cited and there is no cycle.
